title: Lab 6 - Deploy to dev, staging and production
description: Environments, an SSH deploy with a File variable, manual gates, protection and rollback.
scenario: Deploy the published image to a Docker host over SSH as tracked environments, gate staging and production, protect production, and roll back once.
environment_setup:
# A gitlab.com account (free tier is enough) with shared runners enabled on the project,
# git on your machine, and a terminal. Keep Build → Pipelines open in a second tab.
git --version
git remote -v
cleanup: # Nothing to clean: pipelines and jobs are history. Delete the scratch project when the track is over.

tasks.title: Task 1 - Dev environment
tasks.instructions: Store SSH_PRIVATE_KEY (File, protected) and SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS (File). Add deploy-dev with environment name dev + url, pulling the SHA image on the server and restarting the container; end with a health check.
tasks.solution:
ssh -i "$SSH_PRIVATE_KEY" deploy@host "docker pull $IMAGE && docker rm -f app || true && docker run -d --name app -p 3000:3000 $IMAGE"
wget -qO- "$CI_ENVIRONMENT_URL/healthz"
tasks.verification: Operate → Environments lists dev with a deployment and an Open button that answers.

tasks.title: Task 2 - Manual staging
tasks.instructions: Add deploy-staging (when: manual, allow_failure: false) with resource_group: staging and an environment-scoped DEPLOY_HOST.
tasks.solution:
rules:
  - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
    when: manual
    allow_failure: false
tasks.verification: The pipeline blocks at deploy-staging until played; two quick plays queue, not overlap.

tasks.title: Task 3 - Protected production
tasks.instructions: Create deploy-prod on tags only, protect branch main and tags v*, protect environment production with required approval from you, tag v0.1.0.
tasks.verification: A feature-branch pipeline cannot deploy to production; the tag pipeline's deploy-prod asks for approval before it can be played.

tasks.title: Task 4 - Rollback
tasks.instructions: Tag v0.1.1 with a visible change, deploy, then use Rollback on the v0.1.0 row in the production environment.
tasks.verification: The old deployment's job re-runs and the health endpoint serves v0.1.0's response.
